candidates.attacker_control: HTTP request data: (1) the `from` request parameter in AuthenticationProcessingFilter2.determineTargetUrl (line 50), read on the login submission to /j_acegi_security_check; (2) the `pattern` (or legacy `path`) query parameter in DirectoryBrowserSupport.serveFile (lines 160-163); (3) the `redirectTo` submitted-form field in ParametersDefinitionProperty._doBuild (line 160, via JSONObject formData). In all three cases the value is passed to StaplerResponse.sendRedirect/sendRedirect2 after only the weak `isSafeToRedirectTo` test.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The guard does block `//host` and colon-absolute URIs, so only backslash/derived forms are affected. The missing helper is referenced only in javadoc, so its absence does not break compilation and could be a documentation defect rather than a removed check; however the accompanying `@RestrictedSince("1.651.2 / 2.TODO")` annotation is chronologically impossible for a genuine 1.625.4-SNAPSHOT tree, indicating the file was edited. AuthenticationProcessingFilter2 strips the context path only when the value starts with it (line 61-62); with empty/other context paths the raw value survives. No test exercises isSafeToRedirectTo/isAbsoluteUri in the snapshot, and no runtime redirect was exercised.
candidates.impact: Open redirect / post-login phishing: victims can be sent from the trusted Jenkins origin to an attacker-controlled site (e.g. after authenticating), which facilitates credential theft, session/cookie theft via look-alike pages, and abuse of user trust. It also defeats the stated intent of the `isSafeToRedirectTo` call sites (their comments say "avoid open redirect"). No code execution or data read is demonstrated; severity is bounded to redirect/phishing.
candidates.prerequisites: DirectoryBrowserSupport: the viewer must be allowed to reach a workspace/artifact/userContent browse page (e.g. Item.WORKSPACE for AbstractProject.doWs, line 1906-1925; doUserContent has no explicit check at Jenkins.java:3327-3329). ParametersDefinitionProperty: a POST with build rights and valid crumb. Login path: a victim with an account has to log in via a crafted link/page; the attacker does not need an account. Browser-side WHATWG backslash-to-slash normalization for special schemes (and following the Location header) is required for the redirect to leave the Jenkins origin.
candidates.root_cause: hudson.Util.isSafeToRedirectTo (core/src/main/java/hudson/Util.java:1478-1480) is documented as the guard that prevents redirects to absolute/scheme-relative URIs, but its body is only `!isAbsoluteUri(uri) && !uri.startsWith("//")`. `isAbsoluteUri` (lines 1467-1473) looks for ':' before '#', '?' or '/', so it misses backslash forms that browsers normalize to a network-path reference. The deprecated `isAbsoluteUri` javadoc at lines 1462-1466 points callers to `isAbsoluteOrSchemeRelativeUri`, which is absent from the entire source tree (confirmed via search and the P1 symbol index), and the `@RestrictedSince("1.651.2 / 2.TODO")` annotation at line 1465 references a release later than this 1.625.4-SNAPSHOT tree. The missing normalization/backslash check is therefore not applied at any of the three redirect call sites that rely on this helper.
candidates.title: Open redirect: Util.isSafeToRedirectTo fails to treat backslash URLs as scheme-relative
candidates.trace: Attacker supplies e.g. `from=/\evil.com` (or `\\evil.com`) to the login flow. AuthenticationProcessingFilter2.determineTargetUrl reads it (line 50), calls Util.isSafeToRedirectTo (line 56): isAbsoluteUri returns false (no ':' at all) and `startsWith("//")` is false, so the guard returns true; with empty or non-matching context path the raw value is returned (lines 61-66) and Acegi redirects the browser to that value after successful authentication. Equivalently, DirectoryBrowserSupport.serveFile redirects to `pattern=/\evil.com` at lines 163-164, and ParametersDefinitionProperty._doBuild redirects to a `redirectTo` value at lines 160-163. Browsers normalize the leading `\` (or `/\`) to `//`, turning the value into a scheme-relative URL `//evil.com`, i.e. an off-site navigation.
candidates.unverified: Browser normalization of `\` to `/` and the resulting off-site navigation were not tested; the exact Acegi redirect call (sendRedirect/encodeRedirectURL) is library code outside the snapshot, so header emission was not verified. Reachability/authorization for the DirectoryBrowserSupport and _doBuild paths depends on the viewer's rights. Whether this tree is the dataset's genuine upstream snapshot or was modified could not be diffed (no network/upstream access), so the 'removed helper' inference rests on the internal javadoc/annotation inconsistency.

coverage_summary: Scope reported by get_source_scope: 8,829 model-visible files (no symlinks/sensitive-name exclusions), Java-heavy repo (948 indexed Java files, 470 files omitted from the P1 index). The P1 index provides syntax-only containment/call/inheritance candidates, no control-flow or data-flow and no semantic resolution, so all reachability statements above are manual, line-level source reads. I inspected security (ACL, SidACL, crumb issuer, security realm, AuthenticationProcessingFilter2, s2m whitelist, ApiTokenProperty), CLI (commands, CLIAction, CliManagerImpl, Connection), model (DirectoryBrowserSupport, View, ItemGroupMixIn, ParametersDefinitionProperty, FileParameterValue, User/Job-adjacent code), util/file code (Util, FilePath, XStream2, VirtualFile, UpdateSite/JSONSignatureValidator), Jenkins.java endpoints, and ran targeted greps for deserialization sinks, redirect usage, permission checks and path traversal. Priority review rather than exhaustive line-by-line coverage of all 8,829 files. No code was executed and no external services were queried.
limitations: No runtime, browser or exploit testing was performed; the redirect behavior and browser backslash normalization are deduced from source and browser specifications, not verified in this environment.

No upstream/patched copy could be consulted (no network), so the claim that code was removed is inferred from the dangling `isAbsoluteOrSchemeRelativeUri` reference and the anachronistic `@RestrictedSince("1.651.2 / 2.TODO")` annotation.
P1 relation index is partial (470 files omitted) and implements no control/data flow, semantic resolution or reachability; index edges/facts were used only for navigation.
`.jelly` view files and similar presentation resources are not visible/readable in this snapshot, so the login form's propagation of the `from` field could not be verified directly.
The review prioritized security-relevant code paths; large areas (build/SCM execution, plugin loading internals, most UI/model helpers) were sampled rather than fully audited.
Only one candidate is allowed by the review format, so other unconfirmed leads are listed as rejected leads rather than separate candidates.

rejected_leads.lead: jenkins/model/Jenkins.java:3173-3175 doLoginEntry uses `from.startsWith("/")` before sendRedirect2, which likewise admits `/\evil.com`.
rejected_leads.reason: Related open-redirect pattern but a legacy-realm-only, separate guard; not the same root cause and not needed for the selected candidate (kept as a related observation, not a second candidate).

rejected_leads.lead: hudson/FilePath.java:2273-2308 readFromTar builds `new File(baseDir, te.getName())` without rejecting `..` entries, so tar entries could escape the extraction base.
rejected_leads.reason: In-tree callers are internal build/plugin paths (untarFrom/untar/installIfNecessary), attacker control over the archive is unproven and no entry-name filtering is expected in this era; lower evidence and impact than the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: hudson/cli/CLIAction.java:102-127 establishes a CLI channel over HTTP without requiring permission (`do not require any permission to establish a CLI connection`).
rejected_leads.reason: The channel is marked restricted for non-admins (line 114) and remoting ClassFilter.DEFAULT/ObjectInputStreamEx are in use; no missing guard could be pinned to a specific line, so no candidate-level evidence.
Historical API fallback; real authorization is enforced by checkPermission(Item.CREATE) at the create/copy call sites in ItemGroupMixIn (lines 225, 262, 313), so this is not an injected bypass.
SECURITY-247/SECURITY-105 defenses are intact and reference ClassFilter.DEFAULT; no weakening found.
Uses MessageDigest.isEqual for comparison and the MD5/salt construction is the historical design; a hardening opportunity, not a source-verified vulnerability.

summary: Reviewed the Jenkins core snapshot (tree versioned 1.625.4-SNAPSHOT; 8,829 visible files, ~948 Java files in the P1 index) as a defensive source review. Inspected security, CLI, model, util, update/plugin, console and file-serving code, plus grep sweeps for deserialization sinks, redirect helpers, permission checks and path handling. One distinct candidate stands out with strong source evidence: `hudson.Util.isSafeToRedirectTo` only rejects colon-absolute and literal `//` URIs and therefore returns `true` for backslash-normalized scheme-relative forms (`\\evil.com`, `/\evil.com`), which the three in-repo callers then hand to `sendRedirect` with attacker-influenced values (login `from`, directory-browser `pattern`/`path`, parameterized-build `redirectTo`). Internal evidence that this guard was weakened: the deprecated `isAbsoluteUri` javadoc says to use `isAbsoluteOrSchemeRelativeUri` "if your goal is to prevent open redirects", but that method does not exist anywhere in the tree, and the `@RestrictedSince("1.651.2 / 2.TODO")` annotation references a release later than this snapshot's version. Impact is an open-redirect/phishing weakness (CWE-601), not code execution; exploitation was not run.
